member.name: T:BimGo.Clashes.ClashEngine
member.summary:
Clash detection (Round C). Built to stay cheap at scale and to cost nothing until asked:
Broad phase: sweep and prune over the items' boxes along the axis the model spreads most (clearance tests grow each box by half the distance), keeping only pairs that can belong to the test.
Pairs skipped: an element with itself, a host with its hosted inserts (, same model).
Narrow phase (in parallel): each element's triangles inside the pair's overlap box (large elements keep a small triangle tree for the run), then a second sweep over those triangles' boxes and exact triangle tests ().
Hard depth is an estimate: the narrowest width of the crossing outline over the axes and the crossing faces' normals; when that is within the tolerance, corners of one element lying inside the other deeper than the tolerance still make it a clash (a pipe sunk into a slab). Touching faces never clash.
Clearance reports crossings (tagged) and gaps under the distance, with the closest points.
The caches live only for one run.

member.summary: Elements with at least this many triangles get a triangle tree for the run.

member.summary: The trees of one run stop growing past this many triangles in total (memory guard).

member.summary: Corners per element tried by the inside test of a shallow crossing.

member.name: F:BimGo.Clashes.ClashEngine.MAX_CROSSING_POINTS
member.summary: Crossing points kept per pair for the width estimate.

member.name: T:BimGo.Clashes.ClashGeometry
member.summary: Clash geometry (Round C): triangle–triangle crossing with its segment, triangle–triangle distance, point-in-solid. Own implementations of published methods: Möller's interval test for triangle–triangle intersection (Möller, "A Fast Triangle-Triangle Intersection Test", 1997), closest points on a triangle and between segments (the standard region / clamping formulas, as in Ericson, "Real-Time Collision Detection", 2005, ch. 5), Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection (1997) and the even–odd ray parity rule for inside tests. Pure functions, no allocations, thread-safe.

member.summary:
A clash group (Round C, build C-C1; Navisworks style): clashes of one test reviewed together, with its own status, assignee and notes (setting the group's status sets every member's), and one comment / BCF topic for them all. A clash is in at most one group. Members a later run no longer finds stay in the group, resolved; a group is removed only when it has no members left (one member is fine). New clashes stay ungrouped.

member.name: T:BimGo.Clashes.SearchSet
member.summary:
A named group of elements chosen by rules (Round C, stage 1: category / family / type / level / model). An element is in the set when it matches the adding rules (any of them, or all of them with ) and no "not" rule (). A set with no adding rule holds every element (minus the "not" rules). Rules with no value yet are left out.
C-B4: a set can also hold (Revit-filter style AND / OR, one level deep): each group is one more condition, combined with the set's adding rules by . Inside a group every rule is an ordinary condition ("Level is not Level 2" is just false for Level 2 elements); the set's own top-level "not" rules still take elements out of the whole set, as before.

member.name: T:BimGo.Format.BcfFile
member.summary:
Reads and writes BCF files (.bcf; .bcfzip is read too): plain BCF 2.1 out, and 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 in, as far as BimGo's comments need (topic fields, the comment thread, the first viewpoint's camera and selection, its snapshot).
bcf.version VersionId 2.1 project.bcfp project id and name <topic guid>/markup.bcf topic, comments, viewpoint list <topic guid>/viewpoint.bcfv camera, selected components <topic guid>/snapshot.png picture of the viewpoint (PNG: the name and format most viewers expect)
Reading is namespace-agnostic and tolerant: unknown elements are ignored, a damaged topic is skipped (counted) rather than failing the file, DTDs are refused and entry sizes are capped. Never throws.

member.name: T:BimGo.Format.BimGoFormat
member.summary:
Constants and shared serialisation settings for the .bimgo format.
A .bimgo file is a ZIP container (extension masked) holding JSON for metadata and a binary blob for geometry:
manifest.json format version, generator, provenance, extraction settings, counts model.json origin, bounds, site, phase, spawn, levels, rooms, categories elements.json per element metadata and index ranges into geometry.bin parameters.json optional extra parameters (pooled strings) geometry.bin header + SceneVertex[] (28 B each) + uint[] indices, little-endian comments.json comment markers comments/… comment pictures for BCF snapshots (JPEG), referenced from comments.json (optional) journal.json ordered edits (replayed on load; never baked into the geometry) bookmarks.json saved viewpoints and the home viewpoint (optional; only written when there are some) paths.json keyframed camera paths (optional, Round K; only written when there are some) entourage.json billboards: placed trees / people…, imported picture types, their look (optional, Round X-B) entourage/… the imported billboard pictures (PNG), referenced from entourage.json (optional, Round X-B) entourage-slots.json the snapshot's Revit Planting / Entourage instances (optional, Round X-B2) sun.json sun / shadow state: on/off, date, time, intensities (optional) visibility.json hidden categories, links and elements (optional; only written when something is hidden) lighting.json glowing vertex ranges and lighting-fixture lights (optional; only written when there are some) ies/… the fixtures' photometric files (.ies text), referenced from lighting.json (optional, Round X-D1) light-profiles.json per fixture type profile choices and imported .ies files (optional, Round X-D1) materials.json material table for Realistic mode (optional; only when textures were extracted) material.bin header + ushort material index per vertex + float2 surface coordinate (m) per vertex (optional) textures/… embedded texture images (JPEG / PNG), referenced from materials.json (optional) library.json family library: offered family types and the first template vertex (optional; live sessions) library/… family library preview images (PNG), referenced from library.json (optional) rooms.json every room's parameters, pooled, aligned with model.json's rooms (optional, Round Z-A)

Every newer field is optional: older files read as open, normal priority, unassigned, no replies, no view. member.name: T:BimGo.Format.ModelFolders
member.summary:
BimGo's own per-model folders, %LocalAppData%\BimGo\Models\<title>_<hash>\, holding the data a live Revit session keeps between walkthroughs: comments.json, bookmarks.json, sun.json, visibility.json, texture-overrides.json and model.json. Used instead of sidecars beside the model, which is often in the cloud or read-only. A .bimgo file keeps its own copies inside the file.
The key, most stable first: the cloud model GUID, else the workshared central path, else the local path (the Revit side builds it; makes paths case- and slash-insensitive). Two local copies of one model get two folders.
Sharing (optional, off by default): writes are mirrored beside the model, and at each Go a newer file there replaces the folder's copy, so colleagues on a shared drive see each other's comments.
Never throws: failures are logged.

member.name: T:BimGo.Live.FolderChannel
member.summary:
One side of a session's message exchange over two folders: sends into an outbox, receives from an inbox.
Sending writes one per file, atomically (a .tmp file renamed to .json), named so that ordinal file-name order is send order. Receiving uses a plus a slow poll (watchers can miss events), reads files in name order, validates them and deletes them. Received messages queue up for ; fires (on a thread-pool thread) when new ones arrive.
Transport-agnostic callers only use Send / TryReceive, so named pipes could replace the folders later. Thread-safe. Never throws from Send / TryReceive.

member.name: T:BimGo.Live.JournalPush
member.summary:
The app side of pushing a standalone file's journal into a live Revit session (journal.apply).
The app is walking a .bimgo file, not the session, so it must not attach as the session's walkthrough: no app.json is written and no hello is sent. It opens a temporary channel on the session's folders, sends one request and waits for the journal.result with the same request id; anything else arriving in the session's to-app folder meanwhile (model.changed...) is meant for an attached walkthrough, which by definition isn't running, and is discarded.
Game thread only (the channel's watcher runs on its own). Never throws.

member.name: T:BimGo.Live.LiveProtocol
member.summary:
The app ↔ Revit session protocol (version 1): a watched folder per Revit document.
%LocalAppData%\BimGo\Sessions\<sessionId>\ session.json written by Revit: identity, state, heartbeat, latest snapshot app.json written by the attached app: pid, heartbeat to-revit\ app → Revit messages to-app\ Revit → app messages snapshots\ .bimgo snapshots written by Revit (large geometry never travels in messages)
Every message is one JSON file, written atomically (temp file, then rename) and deleted by the reader once handled. Nothing in a message is ever executed; readers validate the session id, the protocol version and the size.

member.name: F:BimGo.Live.LiveProtocol.VERSION

member.name: T:BimGo.Live.LiveSessionSource
member.summary:
The app side of a live Revit session: an whose edits travel to Revit over the session's folders, plus the session extras (). Game thread only, except the channel's own watcher.
Connection health comes from Revit's session.json heartbeat, checked every couple of seconds; the app's own heartbeat (app.json) tells Revit someone is attached. If Revit goes away, waiting edits are answered as failed so the guns put things back, and further edits are refused.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.CameraPathTimeline
member.summary:
The timing and shape of a keyframed camera path (Round K): pure maths, shared by live playback and video recording (stepped at a fixed frame rate).
Shape: a centripetal Catmull-Rom curve through the keys (no cusps or self-loops on uneven key spacing), as Hermite segments whose tangents are scaled by each key's smoothness: 1 is the full curve, 0 a sharp corner (straight runs between keys).
Speed: constant along the curve (an arc-length table per segment maps distance to the curve), at each segment's speed. Where a key eases (it holds, it is an end, or it is set to) the camera speeds up and slows down smoothly (a smoothstep velocity ramp: no jolt).
Time: fade in → key 0 (hold) → segment → key 1 (hold) → … → last key (hold) → fade out; a loop adds the segment from the last key back to the first and has no fades.
Heading: following, the camera looks at the point metres ahead along the path (so it turns progressively, before a corner); a key that holds its own view or looks at a target takes over near itself, blending in over the half segment before it and out over the half after it (the whole segment between two such keys; Round K-C: or, with , out into following and back in). A key holding its own view can pan over its hold (, eased like the tour's swivel).
State: the sun blends from key to key over each segment (); the colour profile switches at a key.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.CoverMap
member.summary:
Round W-B (weather): what covers each spot of the site, seen from above. A grid of cells (about 0.5 m) over the model holding the highest surface's height in each cell, built on the CPU once when rain or snow is first turned on (and again a moment after the shown model changes). Rain and snow stop at it (they fall past windows but never under a roof or a canopy), and the wet and snow looks only reach surfaces that are open to the sky.
Every triangle counts, whatever way it faces: up and down faces by the cells their area covers, and each triangle's edges mark the cells they pass over too (walls, thin members and slivers narrower than a cell).

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.Daylight
member.summary:
Daylight maths (daylight round), pure and allocation-free per call where it matters:
A fixed sky of 192 patches (8 altitude bands of 11.25° × 24 azimuth bins of 15°, scene axes, Z up): rays are binned into patches once per cell, then any sky (overcast, or the clear sky at each time sample) is a 192-term sum.
CIE overcast and CIE clear sky luminance distributions; the clear sky is scaled to the IES clear-sky diffuse horizontal illuminance, and the sun's direct normal illuminance follows the IES extinction formula.
BRE split-flux internally reflected component, reflectance from a colour, and cosine-weighted ray directions.
The results are early design indicators (geometric sky and sun components, one-bounce external reflection, an average internal reflection per room), not a validated simulation such as Radiance.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.GrassField
member.summary: Grass round (build B): where grass grows, seen from above. Grass materials (by keyword) are rasterised into a grid of cells holding the highest grass surface's height and its colour (a small palette), on the CPU, once. Any other upward surface just above the grass (a floor slab on a toposolid, a path, a kerb) takes the cell away, so blades never poke through floors; surfaces well above (roofs, canopies) don't. The app uploads the grid as a texture and places blades around the camera from it.

member.name: F:BimGo.Scene.GrassField.MIN_CELL

member.name: F:BimGo.Scene.GrassField.MIN_UP

member.name: F:BimGo.Scene.GrassField.COVER_BELOW

The level indices to draw on, in elevation order (levels are sorted by elevation), into (cleared first).
Underfoot: just (even when it isn't a building storey: it is where the player is).

Nearest: the level whose elevation is nearest .
Adjacent: below, underfoot and above.
All: every level, or only the building storeys (every level when none is a storey).

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.KeyMap
member.summary:
The live key bindings (input round B2): up to chords per action, starting from the catalogue's defaults with the user's changes on top (settings.json stores only the changes, so a changed default reaches everyone who didn't rebind that action). Answers "did this action fire" for a frame's key state without allocating, finds and swaps clashes, and reads / writes keymap files.
Modifiers. A binding fires when its key goes down while its modifiers are held; extra modifiers don't stop it (Shift+Space still jumps while running) unless another binding live in the same situation uses the same key with more of the held modifiers (Shift+H sets home instead of going home; Shift+1 goes to a bookmark instead of picking gun 1). Held actions (movement, run) ignore that rule.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.LightningStorm
member.summary:
Round W-C: when and where lightning strikes, worked out from the weather clock alone (so a video frame or a photo gets the same storm as the walk), and how bright it is at any moment.
Photosensitive-safety limits, always on: at most three flashes in any second (WCAG 2.3.1): a strike flickers at most three times, at least a third of a second apart, and strikes are at least apart; every flicker rises and falls smoothly (no hard on / off). With reduceFlashing a strike is one slow glow instead (over half a second up, a second and a half down).

member.summary: Round Y-C2: a light profile's polar candela plot (the classic two-plane photometric diagram), as points ready to join with lines. Plot space: the centre at (0, 0), radius 1 = the peak of the two planes, x to the right, y down, so gamma 0 (straight down) is at (0, +r) and a downlight's beam hangs below the centre, as on a data sheet. The C 0–180 plane runs C 0 on the right and C 180 on the left; the C 90–270 plane C 90 right, C 270 left.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.LightProfile
member.summary:
Round X-D1: a light's distribution (how much it sends each way) as the renderer takes it: a small table of relative intensity over the fixture's own angles, plus the scale that keeps its total output at the fixture's lumens.
Angles are IES type C: gamma 0° = straight out of the fixture (nadir for a downlight), 180° = straight back; C 0° along the fixture's "across" axis, 90° a quarter turn anticlockwise seen from behind the light (from above, for a downlight).
The table is gamma rows (0–180° even steps) × C columns (0–337.5°, wrapping), one byte each, peak 255. Bilinear between samples (as the shader does).
= 4π / ∫ table dΩ (peak 1): intensity in units of an even (omnidirectional) light of the same lumens, so swapping a profile never changes how much light a fixture gives, only where it goes.

member.name: P:BimGo.Scene.LightProfiles.BuiltIns
member.summary:
The built-ins, in the order they're offered (made once):
Downlight, narrow: a 25° beam (cos²⁹, half intensity at 12.5°) with a little spill to 60°.
Downlight, medium: a 40° beam (cos¹¹) with spill.
Wide flood: a soft batwing to about 120°, little above the horizon.
Wall washer: down and strongly towards C 0° (aim C 0° at the wall), peaking 35° off nadir.
Pendant: 65 % down (a broad cone), 25 % up, the rest sideways (an opal diffuser).

member.name: M:BimGo.Scene.LightProfiles.FromGeneratedKey(System.String)
member.summary:
A generated profile from its key (made each call: cache it), or null when the key isn't one:
Spot: full intensity inside half the beam angle, a smooth fall to nothing at half the field angle (at least a 2° fall, so a beam equal to its field still has a soft edge), nothing beyond.
Hemispherical: cos γ out of the fixture, nothing behind it.

member.name: M:BimGo.Scene.LightProfiles.Encode(System.Int32,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Packs a profile slot and the fixture's orientation into the negative float the shaders read in place of the downward share (-(code + 1); 24 bits, exact in a float): slot (5 bits) · aim octahedral u, v (6 bits each) · turn about the aim (7 bits). The turn is measured from a reference axis built from the quantised aim (as the shader rebuilds it): world up projected across the aim, or world X when the aim is near vertical.
member.param: C 0°, world (any length; projected across the aim).

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.LunarPosition
member.summary: Round W-A: the moon's place in the sky, its phase, and the frame the stars turn in, from the location, date and local clock time (the same inputs as ). Paul Schlyter's low-precision orbital elements with the main perturbations and topocentric parallax: about a quarter of a degree, plenty for a sky. Pure maths, double precision, no allocations, never throws. Directions use true-north axes (X east, Y north, Z up), as ; azimuths are clockwise from true north.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.OcclusionState
member.summary:
Round Y-D1: which render chunks the main view skips because last frame's occlusion query found nothing of their (slightly enlarged) box in front of the depth already drawn. The renderer owns the GL queries; this class holds the decisions, so they can be tested without a GPU:
A chunk starts visible. A query that finds no sample hides it; one that finds any shows it.
Hidden chunks are queried every frame (so they come back a frame after they show); visible ones every frames, staggered by chunk (fewer queries).
A query not answered yet at the start of a frame keeps its chunk drawn (a slow GPU costs speed, never a hole).
A chunk the camera is near (inside its box grown by ) is always drawn and not queried.
A chunk that leaves the view is forgotten (drawn when it comes back), and its pending answer is ignored.
A jump of the camera (teleport, bookmark, portal: over or a turn over in one frame) shows everything again.
Y-D1 r2: chunks are grouped in clusters (: a m grid, m slabs). When every chunk of a cluster in view is hidden and none waits for an answer, one query of the cluster's box stands in for theirs: no sample keeps them hidden, any shows them all (their own queries then hide the ones still behind something).

member.summary: How much a chunk's box grows for its query (m): a margin for the frame of lag.

member.summary: A chunk whose box (grown by this, m) holds the camera is always drawn.

member.summary: Visible chunks are queried once in this many frames.

member.summary: A move over this in one frame (m) counts as a jump.

member.summary: A turn over this in one frame (degrees) counts as a jump.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.ProxyCatalog
member.summary:
The CC0 proxy keyword list, shared by the Revit add-in (suggestions at extraction) and the app (suggestions in the Textures panel and the image lookup). Only keywords live here: the images ship with the app (Resources/Proxies + proxies.json), never inside a .bimgo.
Suggestion order matters: the first entry with a matching alias wins, so specific entries ("concrete block", "board formed", "carpet tile") come before general ones ("concrete", "tile"). Names that should never get a proxy (glass, mirrors, acoustic ceiling tiles) are caught first by .

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.QualityProfiles
member.summary:
The values each sets, applied to and recognised from a . Shared by the app's pause menu and the Revit Options window so both mean the same thing.
Governed settings: colour mode, anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, shadow quality (whether shadows are on is a per-model choice, O, and is left alone), artificial lights, bloom, reflections (on, tier threshold, sky or probes, probe resolution; X-C1: the Realistic profile's screen-space reflections). Probes HQ is never part of a profile.
Allocation-free: the app recognises the current profile every frame the pause menu is open.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.SolarPosition
member.summary:
Solar position from location, date and local clock time. Ported from Gavin's Pickles.Helpers.SunPosition, with the NOAA "General Solar Position Calculations" series for declination and the equation of time (about 0.01° instead of about 1°). Pure maths, double precision, no allocations, never throws.
Directions use true-north axes: X = east, Y = north, Z = up. turns them into the model's internal axes using the extraction's internal → shared rotation (the same correction as GetRevitSunVector's rotation by −true north).

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.TextureOverrideSet
member.summary:
The texture choices for one Revit host model (and the links extracted with it), remembered per machine in the model's BimGo folder (texture-overrides.json; without a folder, in %AppData%\BimGo\texture-overrides\<host model key>.json). Written by the Revit "Review textures…" window and by the app's Textures panel in a live session; read by every extraction of that model, so a fix made once is used on every Go / F5. Nothing is ever written into the Revit model.
Entries are keyed by document ("host", or a link's model key) and then by material UniqueId, with the material name ("name:…") as a fallback for snapshots that carry no UniqueId.

member.name: T:BimGo.Scene.TourTimeline
member.summary:
The timing of a bookmark tour (tour round): pure maths, shared by live playback and (build A2) video recording, which steps it at a fixed frame rate.
Fade: each stop is fade in (fade s) → hold → fade out (fade s); the stop changes at black. The swivel pans over the whole visible stop, eased in and out.
Glide: the first stop fades in and the last fades out; between stops the camera flies from the end of one stop's swivel to the next stop's view (position, eye height, yaw and pitch, eased). A glide takes at least glide s, longer when the stops are far apart (at most m/s). The swivel pans over the hold.

member.summary: Fastest glide between stops (m/s): far-apart stops glide for longer than the set time.

Where a walkthrough's model lives, and where its edits go. The game submits every edit (demolish, move, clone) here and receives answers asynchronously; it never knows whether Revit is involved.

member.summary: Progress and cancellation shared between a long task and the UI that shows it (possibly on another thread). The task calls for each stage (with the share of the whole bar it covers), then as it goes, and at safe points; the UI polls and calls . Thread-safe and allocation-free per step.
